sources.name: GitHub issues of microsoft/fluentui
sources.version: GitHub REST API 2022-11-28, state as of 2026-11-11
sources.license: GitHub Terms of Service (user content; only facts and our own summaries are kept)

provenance.notes: URL, number, title, state, dates, counts and labels are copied from the API response of each issue. Category, components, summary, resolution and lesson are written by the researcher (tools/extract/field-reports/curation) after reading the issue body returned by the search API and, for the issues listed in docs/research/field-reports.md, the full thread. daysOpen of an open issue is measured to the retrieval date. fixedBy is filled mechanically from merged pull requests that name the issue after a closing keyword. Reports marked needs-review state a cause that the researcher inferred from the symptom without a confirming statement in the issue.

reports.title: Directional icon fonts in IconClassNames are not mirrored in RTL
reports.summary: The design guidance said directional icons should mirror in RTL, but the icon font classes did not, in a product as large as Outlook on the web. It took ten months to close.
reports.lesson: Mirroring is a property of each icon recorded in data and applied by the icon component.

reports.title: mergeStyles: Switching html direction to rtl doesn't change style direction
reports.summary: Styles were flipped according to a direction value captured by the styling library, so switching the html element's direction at runtime did not change already generated styles such as padding-left.
reports.lesson: Generated CSS is direction-agnostic (logical properties); nothing is baked at generation time, so a runtime switch needs no regeneration.

reports.title: FocusZone: bidirectional not working correctly in RTL
reports.summary: In a bidirectional focus zone in RTL, arrow keys did not move focus correctly between items.

fixedBy.title: FocusZone: check for RTL and do correct top to bottom comparisons

reports.lesson: Two-dimensional focus movement applies the RTL swap to the horizontal pair only; table-driven tests cover every orientation in both directions.

reports.title: Support dir=RTL tag on elements other than HTML
reports.summary: The library's RTL logic assumed the direction was declared on the html element; applications that set dir on the body or on a region were not recognised.
reports.lesson: Direction is resolved from the nearest ancestor with a dir attribute (or the provider), never from document.documentElement alone.

reports.title: Positioning issue of Dropdown's options list in RTL context
reports.summary: In an RTL context, when a dropdown's list did not fit, it was always shifted to the right side even when only the left had room.

fixedBy.title: Fix positioning issue of Dropdown's options list

reports.lesson: Collision handling evaluates both physical sides symmetrically; fixture: anchor near each viewport edge in RTL.

reports.title: ColorPicker: full RTL support?
reports.summary: The colour sliders and the colour rectangle made no RTL adjustments; maintainers judged gradient direction less meaningful to users than other directional UI and closed the request after more than two years as not on the roadmap.
reports.lesson: For each value-axis component the RTL behaviour is a recorded decision (mirror or keep), implemented consistently for pointer, keys and visuals.

reports.title: Feature request: Global function to automatically flip icons on RTL
reports.summary: Authors had to pick the left or right variant of an icon by hand after checking the direction; a request for automatic flipping stayed open for seventeen months and was closed without one.
reports.lesson: The icon API takes the logical icon (e.g. chevron-forward) and resolves the glyph.

reports.title: RTL split button style messed up
reports.summary: In RTL the split button's divider and borders were on the wrong sides, and the report sat for almost a year before being soft-closed.
reports.lesson: Split and attached controls use logical borders and radii; screenshot fixture in RTL.

reports.title: The axis of the charts needs to support RTL
reports.summary: The axes of the charting package ignored RTL.

fixedBy.title: added rtl support for all the Cartesian charts

reports.lesson: Charts decide axis mirroring explicitly (y-axis at inline-start, x increasing toward inline-end for categorical data, time axes by policy) and test it.

reports.title: Wrong horizontal gaps between Stack items in RTL mode
reports.summary: Horizontal gaps between stack items were wrong in RTL; an earlier report of the same defect had been closed without the cause being addressed. The stack emulated gaps with margins on one physical side.
reports.lesson: Stack uses the gap property; no margin emulation.

reports.title: Resize details list column in RTL cause the column width to change in the opposite direction
reports.summary: With dir="rtl", dragging a column header's resize handle changed the width in the opposite direction.
reports.lesson: Resize deltas are direction-signed in the shared resize engine.

reports.title: Typing long RTL text in a LTR Text Field doesn't scroll with the text like if you typed LTR text
reports.summary: Typing a long Arabic string into an LTR text field did not keep the caret in view the way Latin text does: the field did not scroll with the text.
reports.lesson: Text inputs set dir="auto" (or the content's direction) where user content may be either direction, and the fixture types long RTL text into an LTR field and checks the caret stays visible.

reports.title: (react-menu) - Menu does not support RTL
reports.summary: With the provider set to RTL, the new menu component's nested submenus were positioned incorrectly.
reports.lesson: Submenu side derives from direction through the shared positioning engine.

reports.title: Fluent Dialog not behaving correctly for RTL direction
reports.summary: With RTL text direction the dialog's parts were misplaced, visible on the documentation site; the report was open for more than a year and soft-closed.
reports.lesson: Documentation examples are rendered in RTL in CI screenshots.

reports.title: Popover, Tooltip: RTL arrow positioning broken
reports.summary: In RTL the arrow of popovers and tooltips disappeared for the logical "before" and "after" positions.
reports.lesson: Arrow placement is computed after logical positions are resolved to physical sides; fixture: arrow visible and pointing at the anchor for all placements × directions.

reports.title: [Bug]: Modal close icon (x) should be placed on the left for RTL
reports.summary: With RTL direction the modal's close button stayed on the right.
reports.lesson: Dismiss buttons sit at inline-end.

reports.title: [Feature]: Auto mirror icons in Fluent UI 9/react-icons 2
reports.summary: In the newer icon package, icons such as an expand-left panel icon had to be swapped by hand for their right-hand counterpart in RTL; a request for automatic mirroring was soft-closed after ten months.
reports.lesson: The mirroring rule supports both transforms (flip) and swaps to a named counterpart.

reports.title: [Bug]: AvatarGroup pie variant breaking in dir="rtl"
reports.summary: The pie variant of the avatar group, which clips and overlaps avatars into one circle, broke under dir="rtl".
reports.lesson: Clip paths and overlaps that are geometric use physical values and are checked in RTL so they are not flipped by accident.

reports.title: [Bug]: fluent-accordion icons spacing broken in RTL
reports.summary: Icon spacing in the web-component accordion differed between LTR and RTL because physical padding and margin properties were used. Open for more than three years.
reports.lesson: Lint rule: no physical inline properties in component styles.

reports.title: [Bug]: fluent-slider does not flip in RTL
reports.summary: The web-component slider does not flip in RTL whether dir is set on the slider or on a parent. Open for more than three years.
reports.lesson: Slider direction is resolved from the DOM and tested with dir on the element and on an ancestor.

reports.title: [Bug]: fluent-tabs keyboard navigation is not flipped in RTL
reports.summary: Keyboard navigation of the web-component tabs is not flipped in RTL. Open for more than three years.
reports.lesson: Roving-focus direction is covered by generated tests for every component using the engine.

reports.title: [Bug]: Drawer animation wrong direction in RTL languages
reports.summary: With the direction set to RTL the drawer animated from left to right. It took six months to fix.

fixedBy.title: fix(react-drawer): add correct animation direction when RTL

reports.lesson: Drawer motion derives from the resolved physical side.

reports.title: [Bug]: Fluent Slider is not honoring RTL direction
reports.summary: A second report that the web-component slider renders left to right under RTL, filed sixteen months after the first, which was still open.
reports.lesson: An open RTL defect in a core input is a release blocker, not backlog.
